one_liner: Pure-Rust PNG/APNG decoder (zune-png) that decodes 1.5x-2.7x faster than an old libspng 0.6.3 build in the maintainer's criterion run.
what_it_does: zune-png decodes PNG and APNG (8- and 16-bit, palette, interlaced) from an in-memory or streaming byte source into a Vec<u8> (decode_raw, 16-bit samples big-endian) or a DecodingResult of u8/u16 in native endianness (decode). It is a Rust crate with its own API (PngDecoder::new(ZCursor), decode_headers, frame_info, more_frames); C callers only reach it through zune-capi (library zil_c, header include/zil.h generated by cbindgen), which wraps the whole zune-image pipeline rather than exposing a libpng- or spng-style decoder. Sub-8-bit images are always expanded to 8 bits and palettes to RGB(A).
how_it_is_fast: The benchmarked dev-branch decoder (rewritten in May 2026) streams IDAT data through zune-inflate's StreamingDecoder, a libdeflate-style table-driven inflater, into a sliding buffer and unfilters each row as soon as it is available, writing straight into the output where no post-processing is needed (two-row ping-pong buffers only for palette/expansion cases). Row unfiltering uses SSE2/SSE4.1 kernels on x86 (sub, avg, paeth; selected by runtime CPU detection with std) and NEON on aarch64 for sub and avg, with paeth there done by an unrolled scalar loop. It also skips work a careful decoder does: the dev decoder never verifies chunk CRC-32 or the zlib Adler-32, regardless of options.
when_to_use: Rust services or tools that decode many ordinary 8-bit RGB/RGBA PNGs and want a dependency-free, no_std-capable decoder (the run shows 135.0 ms vs 149.3 ms for image-rs/png on the baseline image).
Adam7-interlaced 8-bit PNGs: the largest margin in the run (139.7 ms vs 232.8 ms for image-rs/png and 378.0 ms for spng).
APNG playback where you want frame disposal and blending handled for you (ApngContext::process_frame).
Pipelines already using zune-image (JPEG, QOI, HDR, filters) that want one Rust image type with 8/16-bit and f32 support.
when_not_to_use: C or C++ code that wants a libpng/libspng replacement: there is no PNG-level C API, only zune-capi's whole-library zil_* calls built as a Rust staticlib/dylib.
16-bit or palette PNGs: image-rs/png beat zune-png in the same harness (163.7 vs 186.3 ms on 16 bpp; 28.31 vs 35.21 ms on palette).

Untrusted or integrity-sensitive input: the benchmarked dev decoder cannot verify CRC-32 or Adler-32 at all, and issue #221 (52 fuzzer crash files with panics in zune-png, opened July 2024) and #384 (out-of-memory panic) are still open.

Anyone installing from crates.io expecting these numbers: the measured decoder is the unreleased dev branch; zune-png 0.5.2 on crates.io (2026-03-11) is the older whole-buffer decoder on zune-inflate 0.2.54 (2023), which has no StreamingDecoder.
Images wider or taller than 16384 pixels unless you raise max_width/max_height in DecoderOptions.

integration.form: crate (Rust); C access via zune-capi staticlib/dylib (zil_c)
integration.dependencies: zune-core and zune-inflate (workspace crates; zune-inflate pulls simd-adler32 for its zlib feature); no C dependencies
integration.platforms: any Rust target; SIMD unfiltering on x86/x86-64 (SSE2/SSE4.1, runtime-detected with std) and aarch64 (NEON for sub/avg); no_std supported; issue #205 reports the workspace failing to build on i386
integration.thread_safety: not documented; each PngDecoder owns its state, and the PNG path decodes on one thread

gotchas: Checksum options are dead in the benchmarked code: dev-branch zune-png skips every chunk CRC ('png: Remove crc from the PNGChunk') and the streaming inflater never reads the Adler-32, so DecoderOptions::set_strict_mode(true) or png_set_confirm_crc(true) changes nothing for PNG. The released 0.5.2 still honors both options.
decode_raw returns 16-bit samples big-endian; use decode() for native-endian u16, or png_set_strip_to_8bit to drop the low byte.
The benchmark's MiB/s column is compressed input bytes per second (criterion Throughput::Bytes of the PNG file), not decoded pixels.
Build with optimizations even in debug profiles (the README recommends [profile.dev.package.zune-png] opt-level = 3); the intrinsics paths are slow unoptimized.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick zune-png over image-png (Rust png crate) when you are in Rust and mostly decode 8-bit RGB(A) or interlaced images and can live without checksum verification; pick image-png for 16-bit and palette images. From C or C++, libspng (verifies checksums, native C API) or ptpng (1.6x-1.8x over libpng with zlib-ng) are the practical choices.
verified_claims_summary: One first-party criterion run (commit 0875e77, 2026-09-21) on an unnamed Darwin machine, probably Apple Silicon, decoding four images from the maintainer's own test set: zune-png beat the Rust spng 0.1.0 binding (libspng 0.6.3 from 2021, stock zlib, NEON unfilter disabled, CRC still verified) by 2.20x baseline, 2.71x interlaced, 2.9x 16 bpp and 1.5x palette, but it lost to image-rs/png on 16 bpp and palette. The measured zune-png is unreleased dev-branch code that verifies neither checksum, libpng is not measured, and no rustc or C compiler version is given.
status_note: Actively developed (default branch dev, 505 stars, PNG decoder rewritten May 2026, latest benchmark commit September 2026) under MIT, Apache-2.0 or Zlib, but the benchmarked decoder is not yet in a crates.io release.
